newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian state power firm sets Bakun power pact.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian state power firm sets Bakun power pact.

text.p: The Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp (Sesco) has agreed to buy electricity from the Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd for 8.5 cents a unit, the national Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.

The agreement for the purchase was signed in Sarawak's state capital Kuching on Wednesday between Sesco, represented by its managing director , Stephen Wan, and Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Chairman Ting Pek Khiing, Bernama said.
The officials could not immediately be reached for comment.

Under the agreement, Sesco will purchase electricity generated by the Bakun hydroelectric dam, now under construction, at a rate of 8.5 sen per unit for a period of 30 years from the date of full commercial operations.
Ting is also executive chairman of Ekran Bhd, the main contractor of the $5.5 billion Bakun dam, which is being built in the jungles of Sarawak state on Borneo island.
The 2,400 megawatt capacity dam is set to start generating power by 2003.
National utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd last year agreed to purchase power from the dam at a rate of 16.5 cents per unit for the first five years and 17 cents for the next 25 years.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Ting said the cheaper rate offered to Sesco was made possible due to the short distance involved to supply power to Sesco compared with Tenaga Nasional in Peninsular Malaysia, Bernama said.
The power will be sent to the peninsula via a 650-km (400-mile) undersea cable under the South China Sea.
